question.leadin: This outspoken critic of the death penalty executed thousands of political opponents during his reign of power on the Committee of Public Safety.
question.text: Name this "public accuser" who promoted the Cult of the Supreme Being and guillotined [GEE-uh-teen'd] supporters of the monarchy during the "Reign of Terror."
question.answerHtml: Maximilien Robespierre [“robes”-p’yair] (or Maximilien François Marie Isidore de Robespierre )
question.clue: This leader promoted the Cult of the Supreme Being and secured power after the death of his former ally Georges Danton.

swap.leadin: Give the following about Belgian involvement in World War II.
swap.text: The invasion of Belgium by German forces was part of their plan to bypass this series of fortifications on the Franco-German border.
swap.clue: Army Group C conducted a holding action at this place, which allowed Army Groups A and B to move north and then west in the sickle-slice maneuver.

question.text: An apocryphal legend says that the Rothschild banking family profited from a few hours' advance notice of the Duke of Wellington's victory at this 1815 battle, the final defeat of a certain French emperor.
question.clue: The absence of General Grouchy deprived the losers of one third of their army.

swap.leadin: This person was granted an audience with the king after predicting the outcome of the Battle of Rouvray.
swap.text: Name this woman, nicknamed the Maid of Orleans, burned at the stake in 1431 for heresy after fighting for the French against the English at battles such as Patay and the siege of Jargeau.
swap.clue: Guillaume de Flavy stranded this figure outside the gates of Compeigne by lifting a drawbridge too soon, allowing John of Luxembourg to capture this leader, who was then subjected to a trial led by Bishop Pierre Cauchon.

question.text: This protege of Cardinal Richelieu served as Louis XIV's chief minister. He defeated anti-monarchical forces during the Fronde Rebellion and later negotiated the Peace of the Pyrenees.
question.clue: This clergyman succeeded Richelieu as chief minister of France and was an important adviser to Anne of Austria, regent during Louis's youth.

swap.leadin: An army mobilized to fight in this battle after hearing of the raid on the Abbey of Saint Martin.
swap.text: Name this 723 victory for Charles Martel over Abdul Rahman's Umayyad (oo-MAI-ed) forces.
swap.clue: Alessandro Barbero declared that this battle was not an invasion, but merely an attempt to raid the Abbey of St. Martin nearby.

question.leadin: This people was divided into two primary groups: the Ripuarians and the Salians.
question.text: Name this Germanic people that gives their name to the modern-day nation that contains the city of Marseilles.
question.clue: Another ruler of these people waited a year to smash in the head of a man who crushed a bishop's vase.

swap.leadin: This man clashed with Odo the Great over control of Aquitaine, but worked with him during one battle.
swap.text: Name this Frankish leader who defeated an Umayyad army at the Battle of Tours. His nickname means "hammer."
swap.answerHtml: Charles Martel [prompt on Charles , do not accept or prompt on "Martel"]
swap.clue: This man defeated Chilperic II and Eudes in a series of battles which gave control of Neustria and Burgundy to the Mayor of the Palace.

question.leadin: This party signed the Matignon Accords, mandating two weeks of paid annual leave for all workers, and induced auto-makers to develop better cars to compete with German manufacturers by sponsoring the "Million Franc Race."
question.text: Name this alliance of various left-wing parties that controlled France from 1936 to 38 during the premiership of Leon Blum.
question.clue: Meetings that this government conducted with trade unions resulted in the Matignon accords, which granted a 40-hour work week.

swap.text: A king of this name, known as the Quarreller, ruled Navarre in the early fourteenth Century. Kings of this name from another country include ones known as "The Fat" and "The German."
swap.clue: That king of this name went on the Second Crusade and was the first husband of Eleanor of Aquitaine.

question.text: A "passionate" man of this pastoral profession begins a poem by Marlowe with the famous line, "Come live with me and be my love."
question.answerHtml: <u>shepherd</u> (Orlando readers, feel free to repeat “what’s his profession” to confused faces)
question.clue: The Lepers' Plot benefitted from the chaos spread by a 1320 crusade organized after a member of this profession received a biblical vision. A similar crusade named for this profession began after a Hungarian monk was told in a Marian apparition to rescue Louis IX.

swap.text: This monk is popularly, but wrongly, credited with the invention of the traditional method, since they were actually attempting to stop the second fermentation in their wines. This does not prevent Moet et Chandon from naming one of their wines after them.
swap.clue: This French Benedictine monk is often miscredited for the invention of champagne in the 17th century. Regardless, he names a high-sought after brand of champagne sold by Moet & Chandon.

question.leadin: This government was brought about in part by the resignation of the Guizot [gee-ZOH] cabinet.
question.text: Name this government, which was established after an uprising called the June Days brought down the July Monarchy. It lasted only three years.
question.clue: The self-coup that brought down this government prompted the remark that history repeats itself "the first time as tragedy, the second time as farce."

swap.text: This man, who succeeded his father Phillip II Augustus, was the first Capetian not to be crowned during his father's lifetime. His brief rule from 1223 to 1226 saw the renewal of the Albigensian Crusade, and his successor was canonized.
swap.clue: After Magna Carta was signed, John's quarrel with the barons continued until this foreigner signed the 1217 Peace of Lambeth. As a ruler of a non-England place, this person forbade ministers from recording debts owed to Jews and prosecuted a campaign against Count Raymond VII to restore royal authority.

question.text: Increasing exemptions for clergy, nobles, and city dwellers caused great resentment over this largest tax in monarchial France.
question.clue: This French land tax that roughly corresponds to the English tallage. It was placed on peasants from the 1300s to the 1700s.

swap.leadin: A series of mass executions by drowning in this city's Loire ("lwahr") River led to the river being nicknamed the "national bathtub."
swap.text: Name this city in Western France. Pope Clement VIII claimed that a law signed in this city "crucified [him]." The Edict of Fontainebleau ("fon-ten-BLOW") revoked that law.
swap.clue: A series of massacres took place in this city in 1793 when priests were loaded into (+) barges that were then intentionally sunk.

question.leadin: The early Shakers were apparently inspired in part by these black-shirted Huguenot radicals.
question.text: Name these irregular Huguenot insurgents from the Cevennes mountains. Their uprising occurred parallel to the War of the Spanish Succession.
question.clue: This group of Huguenots that rebelled against Louis XIV in southern France.

swap.leadin: Name these people or things associated with the Normandy campaign of 1944.
swap.text: This Norman town gave its name to a "gap" through which in August much of the German army retreated before Polish and Canadian troops closed it, thus trapping 50,000 Germans in the town's namesake "pocket."
swap.clue: After advancing through the initial Norman bocage, or shrubbery, Allied forces encircled most of Army Group B in a pocket named for this town.

question.leadin: He and his brother Louis were executed by Henry III's bodyguard, informally known as "the Forty Five."
question.text: Name this Frenchman that was sponsored by Philip II to keep Henry III Navarre off the thrown when he formed the Catholic League and fought in the War of the Three Henrys.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about military leaders who led their countries during part of WWII, FTPE.
swap.text: This French WWI veteran led the Vichy regime during most of WWII; after the war, he was sentenced to death, but the sentence was mutated into life imprisonment instead.
swap.clue: This man replaced his country's motto with the slogan "Work, family, fatherland" and was influenced by the ideas of Charles Maurras in implementing the National Revolution.
